title: Automate model artifact signing, profile validation, and pinned-version promotion pipeline
creator: Mariana Soto
description:
Background:
Redwood needs an automated CI/CD path that takes a newly-built model artifact through signing, performance profile validation, and promotion to a pinned model version in the model catalog. Current onboarding is partially manual: dev uploads artifacts, writes a profile, and an operator signs/promotes. This causes delays and occasional mismatches between published profiles and runtime artifacts.

Goal:
- Provide a reliable, auditable pipeline that: builds inference artifacts, generates SBOMs, signs artifacts with KMS-backed keys, runs automated performance and correctness validations against canonical workloads, publishes verified performance profiles, and promotes the model to a pinned-version in the catalog only when gating criteria pass.
- Reduce manual steps to zero for trusted CI runs; provide clear override and rollback paths for operators.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- End-to-end pipeline completes on PRs that tag a candidate model artifact and emits a signed artifact bundle and profile JSON into the model-catalog bucket with immutable versioned key.
- Signed manifest + SBOM verified by runtime pull path before deploy; runtime rejects unsigned or mismatched checksums.
- Profile publishing is atomic with the promotion step; if profile validation fails, promotion is blocked and SNS alert created.
- Audit trail includes GitHub PR link, build ID, cosign signature reference, and evaluation metrics snapshot.

Proposed workflow (CI/CD):
1) Build stage (runtime repo action): build model artifact, export weights archive, generate SBOM (syft), and compute checksums. Outputs: model-{hash}.tar.gz, sbom-{hash}.json, manifest-{hash}.json.
2) Unit & Integration tests: smoke inference (small example), model schema validation, quantization-check if applicable.
3) Perf validation job (ephemeral infra): run perf harness on a tiny canary cluster (1 GPU) using curated prompt set. Collect latency P50/P95/P99 and throughput metrics; compute quality metrics (accuracy / nll / custom evals).
4) Profile validator: compare metrics against baseline thresholds for the model family. If within tolerance, generate performance profile JSON (including batching/kv/prefetch suggestions).
5) Artifact signing: sign manifest and profile using cosign integrated with KMS/HSM. Store signature references in the artifact metadata.
6) Promotion: on successful validation and signature, pipeline publishes the artifact + profile to model-catalog (versioned path) and updates 'pinned_versions' index via the catalog service using a transactional update.
7) Canary rollout: optionally trigger an automated canary that routes 1% of traffic to the pinned model for 24h and compares telemetry to baseline; rollback if regressions exceed thresholds.

CI Jobs and gating details:
- Job names: build-artifact, gen-sbom, smoke-infer, perf-canary, profile-validator, cosign-sign, publish-and-promote, canary-observe.
- Each job emits provenance metadata into a normalized artifact-metadata.json that includes the PR, build URL, builder commit, and KMS key fingerprint.
- Promotion is gated: requires (a) profile_validator PASS, (b) cosign-sign success, (c) no open critical findings from SBOM scan.
- Human override: a protected GitHub workflow dispatch that requires two approvers from the Security/Runtime groups - only for emergency promotions.

Security & compliance:
- Use cosign with KMS-managed keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and store key fingerprints in the internal key registry.
- Produce a signed SBOM and run a dependency vulnerability scan; failing findings block promotion and create a ticket with details.
- Store signed artifacts in an immutable, versioned S3/GCS bucket with restricted write permissions to the promotion service principal.
- Audit logs: every promotion event must record user/CI principal, timestamp, artifact hash, and signatures.

Runtime integration & verification:
- Runtime will fetch the signed manifest and verify cosign signatures against the trusted keyset before loading models.
- If profile JSON mismatches the runtime-extracted model metadata (e.g., different sequence length) runtime rejects the load and falls back to the previous pinned model.

Observability and rollbacks:
- Publish evaluation snapshots to the model-metrics store (dataplane) with a link from the artifact metadata.
- Canary-observe job computes drift metrics and opens an incident if QoS regressions detected.
- Promotion is atomic; promotion failures should not leave half-written pinned index entries. Implement via catalog service transaction (DB-backed) and object versioning.

Migration plan for existing models:
- Write a migration script that re-ingests existing model bundles, generates SBOMs, verifies current binaries, signs manifests using the KMS key, and creates profile-placeholder entries flagged 'legacy-import' requiring manual verification.

Implementation notes & decisions made so far:
- Chosen signing tool: cosign (security review prefers sigstore family).
- SBOM generator: syft (well-known and scriptable).
- Perf canary infra: use ephemeral Dedicated-spot pool to limit cost; profile validator runs against a fixed shape to keep results comparable.
- Profile schema v2: includes 'recommended_batch', 'kv_cache_strategy', 'seq_len_distribution', and 'latency_bucket_targets'. Backend schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/1123

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Where to run perf validation for reproducibility vs cost: full-sized Dedicated vs small canary cluster. We chose small canary cluster + conservative thresholds to reduce cost but accept slightly noisier measurements.
- Signature lifecycle: rotating KMS keys will require re-signing pinned artifacts; need a re-signing job and a migration window.
